raw_response:
I will think through this like I always do — start from what I did last year and what my neighbors do. I have 14 mu. My main crop is cotton like it says, but I also keep some land for wheat then maize after, because the family needs grain and selling all cotton is risky if price drops.

I will plant cotton on 8 mu — that is the best land, flat and near the well. The other 6 mu I will do winter wheat then summer maize, two crops on same land. This way I have food, feed for anything we raise, and cash from cotton.

**Cotton (8 mu):** I buy improved seed from the town dealer, the Bt kind — the bollworm trouble is much less with it, everyone around me uses it now. I plant end of April. For fertilizer I put 2 bags of compound fertilizer (50 kg bags, so about 100 kg) per mu as base before planting — that is around 15 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, 7 kg potassium per mu. Then at bud stage I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu, about 10 more kg nitrogen. Cotton is hungry, if I give too little the bolls are small. Water from the well 4 times — before planting, at bud, at flower, at boll. Spraying is the big job — aphids early, then mirid bugs, then still bollworm some, plus weeds. I spray maybe 7 times the whole season. I plough the field deep before planting because cotton likes deep soil. Last year I got about 270 kg seed cotton per mu, I expect same.

**Wheat (6 mu, winter):** I plant October. Seed is improved variety from the seed station, what the neighbors use. Two bags compound fertilizer per mu as base — 14 kg N, 7 kg P, 5 kg K. Then in spring at jointing I topdress one bag urea per mu, another 10 kg N. Irrigate 3 times — winter water, spring green-up, grain filling. Spray 2 times, once for aphids, once for wheat rust if I see it. Rotary till before planting, saves time. I expect 450 kg per mu, last year was about that.

**Maize (6 mu, summer after wheat):** Right after wheat harvest I plant hybrid seed — Zhengdan or similar, whatever the dealer has that year that neighbors liked. No tillage, just direct seed into the wheat stubble, saves money and time. One bag compound fertilizer at planting, then one and a half bags urea at big trumpet stage — so about 12 kg N base plus 17 kg N topdress, total 18 kg N, 5 kg P, 4 kg K per mu. Water 2 times if the rain is not enough. Spray 1 time for corn borer. Expect 550 kg per mu.

I spend carefully but I do not skimp on fertilizer — losing yield costs more than the extra bag.
